properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 8 at 10:49AM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 88 to 100 expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...From 8 AM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Humid conditions will add to heat discomfort.
Heat peaking on Wednesday for most areas.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 8 at 1:49AM MDT until September 8 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From 11 AM MDT this morning through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations
downstream of the South Fork and Salt wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Monsoon moisture and atmospheric instability will be present this
afternoon, leading to the development of strong, slow- moving
thunderstorms over the Sacramento mountains. These slow-moving
storms will be capable of producing rainfall rates of 1 to 2
inches per hour which may lead to excessive runoff on the
vulnerable South Fork and Salt burn scars. These burn scars are
very susceptible to flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 8 at 1:10PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
At 110 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Covington, moving northwest at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Winds in excess of 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Hammond, Mandeville, Covington, Ponchatoula, Abita Springs,
Madisonville, and Robert.

This includes the following Interstates...
Interstate 12 between mile markers 39 and 65.
Interstate 55 in Louisiana near mile marker 29.
properties.instruction:
Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 8 at 9:23AM CDT until September 8 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM MDT /7 PM CDT/ THIS EVENING
DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF CENTRAL AND
NORTH CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA...

The National Weather Service in Aberdeen SD has issued a Red Flag
Warning.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of central and north central South Dakota.

* TIMING...Until 7 PM CDT /6 PM MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...West winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 18 to 28 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.
